newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates stable, demand grows.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates stable, demand grows.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were stable on Friday as banks increased demand for funds because o;f end-of-week corporate tax and pension payments, dealers said.
"Demand is huge and we ran out of funds on offer so we had to beg banks for money," one dealer said. She said 15 million kuna in demand was still unmatched.
"Payments for pension funds are emptying banks' deposits," she said.
Fresh settlements totalled 39.9 million kuna most of which were call money loans granted at un unchanged 8.0 percent. A few call money loans were struck at 9.0 percent.
One-month money was granted at 15 percent and a smaller 10-day loan was made at 11 percent.
Commercial banks had 14.2 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from Thursday's 7.5 million. Banks lent each other 2.9 million kuna in direct off-market trade to square their positions.

Overnight trade totalled 33.3 million kuna, as one bank with shortfalls borrowed 5.4 million kuna and the rest went to five banks to keep up their mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
